issues.title: M-01
issues.summary: The runtime auto-resolves and installs the third-party 'smithers-orchestrator' workflow engine with a floating semver range and no committed lockfile, then executes its binary with the caller's entire environment (including provider API keys) under the skip-permissions trust model. This combines SKILL sections 8.1/8.2/8.5 (outdated/unpinned dependencies, missing integrity/lockfile) with code execution (CWE-1357, CWE-494, CWE-829, CWE-829).
issues.evidence: packages/runtime/src/init.ts:187-204 generates .smithers/package.json pinning "smithers-orchestrator": "^0.27.0", "zod": "^4.4.3", and devDependency "typescript": "^6.0.3" (a range with no currently-published 6.x, underscoring the non-reproducible ranges). packages/runtime/src/smithers.ts:503-529 (ensureSmithersDependencies) runs execFileAsync("npm", ["install", "--prefix", packageRoot, "--no-audit", "--no-fund", ...]) — plain `npm install`, not `npm ci`; `git ls-files` shows no tracked .smithers lockfile and .gitignore excludes .smithers/, so the first install resolves the range non-deterministically with no shared integrity pin. The freshly installed binary is then launched via execFileAsync(executable, command, { env: smithersCommandEnv(...) }) at smithers.ts:410-424, and smithersCommandEnv (smithers.ts:552-562) returns { ...process.env, ...env } — the full parent environment. docs/security.md:24-26 confirms there is no network allowlist or sandbox around agent execution.
issues.mitigation: Commit and install from a lockfile for the generated .smithers workspace (use `npm ci` against a checked-in package-lock.json, or pin an exact smithers-orchestrator version and verify its integrity hash). Avoid floating ranges (drop the caret; the `typescript ^6.0.3` entry should be corrected to a resolvable pinned version). Consider vendoring or pinning-by-digest the workflow engine and re-enabling `npm audit` in the install step.

issues.title: L-01
issues.summary: The dashboard session token that authorizes all privileged mutations (run, materialize, clean, config/topology/prompt edits) is returned by GET /api/session, an endpoint gated only by loopback checks and not by the token itself. Any local user or process able to reach the loopback port can read the token and then drive privileged operations (SKILL 9.1 missing authentication on a sensitive endpoint; CWE-287, CWE-522, CWE-200).
issues.evidence: packages/dashboard/src/index.ts:187-195 (handle) applies only requireLocalRequest() to /api/* routes. The session route at index.ts:209-212 returns this.session(), which at index.ts:374-381 includes `sessionToken: this.sessionToken`. requireLocalRequest (index.ts:1553-1566) enforces only loopback Host/Origin and rejects cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site; it does not require the token. Mutations are gated by requireMutation (index.ts:1568-1574) which checks the token, and it protects config PUT (255), topology PUT (266), prompts (299/305/316) and commands POST (335) — but the token needed to pass those checks is freely readable from /api/session. On a shared/multi-user host every local account can therefore obtain it.
issues.mitigation: Do not expose the session token over an endpoint reachable without the token. Bind the token to an out-of-band secret the browser bootstraps from (e.g., a one-time value printed to the operator's terminal / embedded only in the served index.html for the launching user), or restrict the dashboard to per-user socket permissions. Document that the loopback interface must not be used on multi-tenant hosts.

issues.title: L-02
issues.summary: The dashboard HTTP server sets no defensive response headers on the served SPA/HTML or static assets: no Content-Security-Policy, no X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, no X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and no Referrer-Policy (SKILL 3.4 Missing CSP and 7.5 Missing Security Headers; CWE-16, CWE-1021).
issues.evidence: packages/dashboard/src/index.ts:1630-1647 (sendStaticAsset) writes only `content-type` and `cache-control`; startSse (1649-1657) and sendJson (1615-1623) likewise set no security headers. A repository-wide grep for content-security-policy / x-frame-options / x-content-type-options / strict-transport-security / referrer-policy in packages/dashboard/src returned no matches. index.html is served (index.ts:362-365) with no CSP or framing protection.
issues.mitigation: Add a baseline header set to all responses: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` (or CSP `frame-ancestors 'none'`), a restrictive `Content-Security-Policy` (default-src 'self'), and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`. Risk is reduced by React's auto-escaping, loopback-only binding, and the existing Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site anti-CSRF checks, but these headers are cheap defense-in-depth.

issues.title: L-03
issues.summary: Every spawned subprocess (the workflow-runner/agent, `npm install`, and reference `git` operations) inherits the orchestrator's entire environment, including all provider API keys, rather than a scoped credential subset (SKILL section 1 secrets handling / least-privilege; CWE-200, CWE-214).
issues.evidence: packages/runtime/src/smithers.ts:552-562 (smithersCommandEnv) returns `{ ...process.env, ...(env ?? {}) }` and is passed as the child `env` for both agent execution (smithers.ts:418-422) and the runtime `npm install` (smithers.ts:521-525). The Codex agent template also forwards keys (packages/runtime/src/templates/smithers/agents/codex.tsx:15-27 reads OPENAI_API_KEY). Because M-01 executes third-party code in that same environment, any secret present in the shell (e.g., BRAINTRUST_API_KEY, LANGSMITH_API_KEY, cloud creds) is exposed to it.
issues.mitigation: Construct child-process environments from an explicit allowlist (PATH plus only the specific api_key_env the selected agent/profile requires), instead of spreading process.env. This limits blast radius if a spawned tool or dependency is compromised.

issues.title: L-04
issues.summary: CI supply-chain and command-construction hygiene: the target-E2E workflow pipes a remote installer directly to a shell with no integrity check inside a job that authenticates with a real OPENAI_API_KEY, and the E2E driver builds `git clone`/`git fetch` invocations from workflow-supplied repository/ref strings that could begin with `-` (argument injection) (SKILL 8.5 missing integrity check / CWE-494 and SKILL 2.2 command/argument injection / CWE-88).
issues.evidence: .github/workflows/target-e2e.yml:87-95 runs `curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 sh` (with an `npm install -g @openai/codex` fallback) in a job that sets OPENAI_API_KEY from secrets (lines 65-73, 103-106). scripts/ci/run-target-e2e.sh:133-166 derives clone_repository / checkout_ref from the input via normalize_github_target and then calls `git clone --branch "$checkout_ref" ... "$clone_repository"` and `git fetch --depth 1 origin "$checkout_ref"`; inputs that are not normalized to an https URL and contain no '/' are passed through unchanged, so a value beginning with `-` reaches git as an option.
issues.mitigation: Pin the Codex CLI to a version and verify a published checksum/signature before executing (or install only via the pinned npm package). Prefix untrusted git operands with `--` (e.g., `git clone -- "$url" "$dest"`) and reject refs/URLs matching `^-`. Note this workflow is maintainer-gated (workflow_dispatch inputs or a fixed matrix) and fork PRs do not receive secrets, which limits reachability.

issues.title: I-01
issues.summary: The optional evals LLM-judge sends a bearer API key by POST to an endpoint taken from the ULTRAFUZZ_EVAL_JUDGE_URL environment variable with no scheme (https) or host validation, so a misconfigured/overridden endpoint can transmit the credential over cleartext or to an unintended host (SKILL 1.3 / 6.5; CWE-319, CWE-200).
issues.evidence: packages/evals/src/scoring.ts:463-498 (gatewayLlmJudge): apiKey is read from ULTRAFUZZ_EVAL_JUDGE_API_KEY/BRAINTRUST_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY (467-473); endpoint = env.ULTRAFUZZ_EVAL_JUDGE_URL ?? 'https://gateway.braintrust.dev/v1/chat/completions' (474); the fetch at 486-498 sets header `authorization: Bearer ${apiKey}` to that endpoint with no assertion that it is https or an allowlisted host.
issues.mitigation: Validate that the configured judge endpoint uses https and (optionally) matches an allowlist before attaching the Authorization header. Because the endpoint is operator-controlled configuration rather than remote input, exposure is limited to operator misconfiguration.

issues.title: I-02
issues.summary: The dashboard returns raw internal error text (which for filesystem errors can include absolute host paths) to the client, and streams raw error messages over SSE (SKILL 7.2 / 9.6 verbose errors; CWE-209). Impact is minimal because the interface is loopback-only and single-operator.
issues.evidence: packages/dashboard/src/index.ts:1625-1628 (sendError) returns { error: errorMessage(error) }; errorMessage (1971-1973) returns `error.message` verbatim; HttpError messages embed request paths (e.g., 279 `unknown dashboard API route: ${url.pathname}`, 371 `not found: ${url.pathname}`) and underlying fs/ENOENT errors surfaced through this path can include absolute filesystem locations. streamEvents (1342-1356) writes errorMessage(error) to the SSE channel.
issues.mitigation: Return generic messages with a correlation id to the client and log full detail server-side; this is low priority for a localhost-only operator tool but aligns the dashboard with the catalog's error-handling guidance.

reports.reportMarkdown:
# Ultrafuzz — AI Code Security Anti-Pattern Review (method-01)

- **Repository (local checkout):** `/tmp/ultrafuzz-fable-executor/repository`
- **Project:** Ultrafuzz — agentic orchestrator for smart-contract fuzzing (TypeScript, pnpm monorepo)
- **Snapshot commit:** `c727b264eb50ebc2422f26d8f6afe8e962155680` (branch `main`, HEAD), dated 2026-07-13, subject "Upgrade Smithers and require task summaries (#32)"
- **Working tree:** clean (`git status` reports nothing to commit)
- **Method:** method-01 — *AI Code Security Anti-Patterns (Breadth Version)* (`methods/method-01/SKILL.md`, v1.0.0). The full 7,315-line catalog (10 domains, 50+ anti-patterns, Pre-Generation Security Checklist, CWE cross-reference) was read and applied to the authorized checkout.

> This report is private review material. Record titles are opaque (C/H/M/L/I-NN); all detail is in the fields below.

---

## 1. Methodology & scope

The method is a language-agnostic catalog of insecure ("BAD") vs. secure ("GOOD") patterns across ten domains: (1) secrets/credentials, (2) injection (SQL/command/LDAP/XPath/NoSQL/template), (3) XSS, (4) authentication & sessions, (5) cryptographic failures, (6) input validation, (7) configuration & deployment, (8) dependency/supply-chain, (9) API security, (10) file handling. I mapped each domain onto the actual attack surface of this project and gathered evidence with non-destructive inspection only.

Attack surface identified and reviewed:
- **`packages/security`** — path/id policy, materialize/clean policy, secret redaction.
- **`packages/artifacts/src/safe-paths.ts`** — durable/atomic writes, temp files, symlink and traversal guards, hashing.
- **`packages/dashboard/src/index.ts`** (1,981 lines) — the only long-lived HTTP server (local dashboard + JSON API + SSE + in-process command execution) and its React SPA under `packages/dashboard/frontend`.
- **`packages/references/src/index.ts`** — network fetch of pinned references over `git`, cache integrity.
- **`packages/runtime/src/smithers.ts` / `init.ts`** — agent/workflow subprocess execution, dependency install, environment handling, Codex agent template.
- **`packages/config`** — TOML config, env overrides, `api_key_env` indirection.
- **`packages/evals`** — optional LLM-judge and Braintrust/LangSmith reporters (network egress + API keys).
- **CI:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/target-e2e.yml`, `scripts/ci/*`.

Non-destructive checks performed: full git-tracked file enumeration (298 files); repository-wide secret scans (token/AWS/GitHub/JWT/private-key patterns); grep sweeps for `child_process`/shell usage, `fetch`/HTTP servers, crypto/RNG, SQL construction, XSS sinks (`innerHTML`/`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`/`document.write`/`eval`/`new Function`/`vm`), and catastrophic-backtracking regexes; reading of the security-critical source files listed above; and review of the project's own `docs/security.md`.

**Limitations (clearly labelled):** I did not execute the application or run `npm/pnpm audit` (offline, non-destructive scope; `node_modules/` is present but scanners were not run). The third-party `smithers-orchestrator` engine and other external dependency source were treated as out of scope (their trust is exactly the subject of M-01). The React SPA was reviewed for dangerous DOM sinks and framework (React auto-escaping) but not line-by-line for logic bugs. The committed `smithers.db*` files are local, git-ignored runtime SQLite artifacts and were not inspected for content.

---

## 2. Overall assessment

This is a **security-conscious, defensively engineered codebase**. The project ships a dedicated security package and consistently applies the *secure* side of the method's patterns. No exploitable web-class vulnerability (injection, XSS, auth bypass, path traversal, hardcoded secret) was found. The residual findings are supply-chain and defense-in-depth hardening items, all partially mitigated by the explicitly documented "trusted local execution" model (`docs/security.md`).

### Positive controls observed (evidence)
- **No hardcoded secrets.** Secret scans over all tracked files returned only redaction regexes and clearly-synthetic test fixtures (e.g., `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`). Credentials are referenced indirectly by environment-variable *name* via `api_key_env` (`packages/config/src/agents.ts:12`, `ultrafuzz.toml`), matching SKILL §1.1–1.2 GOOD patterns.
- **No shell string-command execution.** All process spawning uses `execFile`/`execFileSync`/`spawnSync` with argument arrays: references git operations (`packages/references/src/index.ts:686,707,726,736`), agent/npm execution (`packages/runtime/src/smithers.ts:418,521`), evals git (`packages/evals/src/utils.ts:219`). This structurally avoids command injection (SKILL §2.2 / CWE-78).
- **Strong path/traversal/symlink policy.** `packages/security/src/path-policy.ts` canonicalizes with `realpathSync.native` and enforces containment (`resolvePathInside`, `isPathInside`); `packages/artifacts/src/safe-paths.ts:77-133,248-265` rejects symlink components and validates real-path containment. Reference and materialize/clean paths are validated (`materialize-policy.ts`). (SKILL §6.6, §10.1, §10.5 / CWE-22/59.)
- **Safe file writes and permissions.** `writeFileDurable` (`safe-paths.ts:159-174`) creates exclusive temp files (`open(..,'wx',0o600)`), fsyncs, and atomically renames; `appendLineDurable` uses `0o600`. This satisfies SKILL §10.4/§10.6 (CWE-377/732).
- **Secret redaction before persistence.** `packages/security/src/sensitive-redaction.ts` redacts key/URL/bearer/provider-token patterns from stored artifacts and diagnostics; applied in `smithers.ts:490-491` (`sanitizedDiagnosticText`). (SKILL §1, defensive logging / CWE-532.)
- **Supply-chain integrity for references.** Reference commits must be full 40-char SHAs (`references/src/index.ts:449-504`), repo owner/name are charset-validated, cached files are verified by SHA-256 digest against a manifest (`index.ts:573-583`), and fetch uses `git ... origin <sha>` with args arrays. (SKILL §8.2/§8.5 GOOD.)
- **Dashboard hardening.** Binds loopback-only (`validateLoopbackHost` `index.ts:1546-1551`; `listen` `1530-1544`); rejects non-loopback Host/Origin and cross-site `Sec-Fetch-Site` (`requireLocalRequest` `1553-1566`); mutations require a 256-bit per-process session token compared with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (`requireMutation` `1568-1574`, `constantTimeEqual` `1589-1593`); commands are restricted to an allowlist (`SUPPORTED_COMMANDS` `93-107`) executed **in-process** (no shell), with `materialize`/`clean` requiring explicit confirmation (`1167-1169`); static assets reject `..`/backslash and enforce `assertPathInside` (`sendStaticAsset` `1630-1647`).
- **No XSS/SQL/dynamic-exec sinks.** No `innerHTML`/`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`/`document.write`/`eval`/`new Function`/`vm` in the SPA or backend; the frontend is React (auto-escaping, `main.tsx`). No SQL is constructed in-repo (the SQLite `smithers.db` is owned by the external engine).
- **Least-privilege CI.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` sets `permissions: contents: read`, installs with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, and the root `pnpm-lock.yaml` is committed (SKILL §8.2). The E2E workflow masks the API key with `::add-mask::`.

---

## 3. Findings

Severity counts: **Critical 0 · High 0 · Medium 1 · Low 4 · Informational 2.** All are anchored to commit `c727b26`.

### M-01 — Runtime auto-install + execution of a floating-range dependency with full inherited environment (SKILL §8.1/§8.2/§8.5; CWE-1357/494/829)
**Where:** `packages/runtime/src/init.ts:187-204`; `packages/runtime/src/smithers.ts:503-529` and `410-424`, `552-562`.
**Detail:** `renderSmithersPackageJson()` emits a `.smithers/package.json` with floating ranges — `"smithers-orchestrator": "^0.27.0"`, `"zod": "^4.4.3"`, and devDependency `"typescript": "^6.0.3"` (a range with no currently-published 6.x, itself a symptom of unpinned specification). `ensureSmithersDependencies()` then runs `npm install --prefix .smithers --no-audit --no-fund` — **plain `npm install`, not `npm ci`** — and no `.smithers` lockfile is tracked (`.smithers/` is git-ignored). The first install therefore resolves versions non-deterministically with no shared integrity pin, and `--no-audit` disables vulnerability checks. The freshly resolved binary is executed with `env: smithersCommandEnv(...)`, which returns `{ ...process.env, ...env }` — the caller's **entire** environment (including all provider API keys). `docs/security.md:24-26` confirms there is no network allowlist or sandbox around this execution.
**Impact:** A malicious or compromised future 0.27.x publish (or maintainer compromise) is silently pulled and executed on the operator's machine with all secrets in scope. This is the canonical supply-chain risk the catalog flags, elevated by code execution + credential-bearing environment.
**Mitigation:** Commit a lockfile for `.smithers` and install with `npm ci`; or pin an exact version and verify its integrity/signature; drop caret ranges (and fix `typescript ^6.0.3`); re-enable `npm audit`; consider scoping the child environment (see L-03).

### L-01 — Session token disclosed to any loopback client via unauthenticated `GET /api/session` (SKILL §9.1/§4.3; CWE-287/522/200)
**Where:** `packages/dashboard/src/index.ts:187-195`, `209-212`, `374-381`, `1553-1574`.
**Detail:** All `/api/*` routes require only `requireLocalRequest()` (loopback Host/Origin + non-cross-site). The `session` route returns `this.session()`, which includes `sessionToken`. That token is what `requireMutation()` requires to authorize privileged mutations — `run` (spawns agents), `materialize` (writes to the repo), `clean` (deletes generated paths), and config/topology/prompt edits. Because the token is freely readable by anything that can reach the loopback port, on a shared/multi-user host any local account can obtain it and drive those operations.
**Mitigation:** Do not serve the mutation token from a token-less endpoint; bootstrap it out-of-band (operator terminal / embedded only in the launching user's HTML) or use per-user socket permissions; document that loopback exposure is unsafe on multi-tenant hosts.

### L-02 — No HTTP security headers on the dashboard (SKILL §3.4/§7.5; CWE-16/1021)
**Where:** `packages/dashboard/src/index.ts:1615-1657` (`sendJson`/`sendError`/`sendStaticAsset`/`startSse`).
**Detail:** Responses set only `content-type`/`cache-control`. No `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, or `Referrer-Policy` are ever emitted (repo-wide grep for these header names in `packages/dashboard/src` is empty). `index.html` is served without CSP or framing protection.
**Mitigation:** Add a baseline header set (`nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`/CSP `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `default-src 'self'`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`). Practical risk is low given React auto-escaping, loopback binding, and existing Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site checks.

### L-03 — Full `process.env` (incl. API keys) propagated to all child processes (SKILL §1; CWE-200/214)
**Where:** `packages/runtime/src/smithers.ts:552-562`, used at `418-422` and `521-525`; `templates/smithers/agents/codex.tsx:15-27`.
**Detail:** `smithersCommandEnv` spreads the entire parent environment into the workflow-runner/agent, the `npm install` of M-01, and (via inheritance) git operations. Every secret present in the operator shell is exposed to each spawned tool.
**Mitigation:** Build child environments from an explicit allowlist (PATH + only the `api_key_env` the selected profile needs).

### L-04 — CI: remote installer piped to shell + un-sanitized git operands (SKILL §8.5/§2.2; CWE-494/88)
**Where:** `.github/workflows/target-e2e.yml:65-106`; `scripts/ci/run-target-e2e.sh:133-166`.
**Detail:** The E2E job runs `curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | ... sh` (with an npm fallback) with no checksum/signature, inside a job authenticated by `secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY`. Separately, `run-target-e2e.sh` derives `clone_repository`/`checkout_ref` from workflow inputs and passes them into `git clone --branch "$checkout_ref" ... "$clone_repository"` / `git fetch origin "$checkout_ref"`; inputs not normalized to an https URL and lacking a '/' pass through unchanged, so a value beginning with `-` reaches git as an option (argument injection).
**Mitigation:** Pin/verify the Codex CLI before executing; prefix git operands with `--` and reject operands matching `^-`. Reachability is limited: the workflow is maintainer-gated (workflow_dispatch inputs / fixed matrix) and fork PRs do not receive secrets.

### I-01 — Eval LLM-judge sends bearer API key to an unvalidated configurable URL (SKILL §1.3/§6.5; CWE-319/200)
**Where:** `packages/evals/src/scoring.ts:463-498`.
**Detail:** `endpoint = env.ULTRAFUZZ_EVAL_JUDGE_URL ?? 'https://gateway.braintrust.dev/...'`; the API key is attached as `authorization: Bearer <key>` in the POST with no assertion that the endpoint is https or on an allowlist. A misconfigured/overridden endpoint can leak the credential (cleartext or unintended host). Operator-controlled configuration, so exposure is limited to misconfiguration.
**Mitigation:** Require https and optionally allowlist the judge host before attaching Authorization.

### I-02 — Verbose error messages returned/streamed by the dashboard (SKILL §7.2/§9.6; CWE-209)
**Where:** `packages/dashboard/src/index.ts:1625-1628`, `1971-1973`, `1342-1356`; e.g. `279`, `371`.
**Detail:** `sendError` returns raw `error.message`; `HttpError` messages embed request paths, and underlying fs/ENOENT errors surfaced through this path can include absolute filesystem locations, also over SSE. Impact is minimal (loopback-only, single operator).
**Mitigation:** Return generic messages with a correlation id and log detail server-side.

---

## 4. Method-checklist coverage summary

- **Secrets/Credentials (§1):** GOOD — env-name indirection, no hardcoded secrets, redaction before persistence. Hardening: scope child env (L-03); validate judge URL (I-01).
- **Injection (§2):** GOOD — no SQL in-repo; all process calls use arg arrays (no shell). Minor CI argument-injection note (L-04).
- **XSS (§3):** GOOD — React SPA, no dangerous sinks; add security headers (L-02).
- **Auth/Session (§4):** Strong (session token, constant-time compare, loopback+CSRF); token-disclosure gap (L-01).
- **Cryptography (§5):** GOOD — SHA-256 for integrity/ids, `crypto.randomBytes` for tokens/ids, `timingSafeEqual`; no weak algorithms, no home-grown crypto.
- **Input validation (§6):** GOOD — strict id/path validators, JSON body type-checks, no ReDoS patterns found.
- **Configuration/Deployment (§7):** GOOD — loopback bind, least-privilege CI; add security headers (L-02); reduce error verbosity (I-02).
- **Dependency/Supply-chain (§8):** Committed root lockfile + reference digest pinning are GOOD; the generated `.smithers` install is the primary gap (M-01); CI installer piping (L-04).
- **API security (§9):** In-process command allowlist + confirmation + ownership-safe path policy are GOOD; sensitive-endpoint auth gap (L-01).
- **File handling (§10):** GOOD — 0o600 durable/atomic writes, exclusive temp files, symlink/traversal guards.

The project's own `docs/security.md` accurately and honestly states the boundaries it enforces deterministically versus those that rely on the trusted-local model; the findings above are consistent with — and hardening opportunities within — that stated model.

issues.title: H-01
issues.summary: A repository-controlled eval profile can select an arbitrary environment variable and transmit its value as a credential to an arbitrary endpoint. A malicious configuration change can therefore exfiltrate unrelated process secrets when an operator runs or publishes an eval.
issues.evidence: The tracked root `ultrafuzz.toml` is loaded for eval commands by `packages/cli/src/command-shared.ts:53-79`. `packages/config/src/loader.ts:381-422` accepts arbitrary strings for `api_key_env`, `workspace_id_env`, and `endpoint`. The resolved configuration schema at `packages/config/src/resolve.ts:49-79` does not constrain eval profiles, and `validateResolvedConfig` at lines 107-114 performs no provider-profile URL or environment-name validation. `packages/evals/src/reporters/index.ts:97-122` reads the configured environment variables and passes both their values and the configured endpoint to the reporter. `packages/evals/src/reporters/langsmith.ts:351-359` sends the selected values to the endpoint in credential headers; `packages/evals/src/reporters/braintrust.ts:359-367` does the same with an authorization header. Neither reporter constructor validates the endpoint. Exploitation requires the operator to invoke a network-publishing eval workflow, but the configured destination is not confirmed or restricted. This also permits requests to loopback, link-local, or other internal HTTP services.
issues.mitigation: Validate provider profiles before any environment lookup or request. Default each provider to an allowlist of its official HTTPS hosts, reject credentials embedded in URLs, and reject non-HTTPS, loopback, private, and link-local destinations unless a separately trusted user-level override explicitly enables them. Do not allow repository configuration to name an arbitrary environment variable; use fixed provider-specific variable names or obtain the value through trusted CLI/user configuration. Display and confirm the final destination host for custom endpoints. Add negative tests for secret-selection, insecure schemes, deceptive hostnames, redirects, and private-network destinations.

issues.title: H-02
issues.summary: Workflow startup automatically installs floating runtime dependencies and then executes a project-local workflow-runner binary based only on its existence. This creates non-reproducible registry execution and permits pre-existing project-local executables or symlinks to run with the operator's privileges.
issues.evidence: `packages/runtime/src/init.ts:187-203` generates `.smithers/package.json` with caret ranges for `smithers-orchestrator`, `zod`, and `typescript`, but does not generate a lockfile or integrity metadata. The repository's `pnpm-lock.yaml` does not cover `smithers-orchestrator`. When the local runner is absent, `packages/runtime/src/smithers.ts:503-525` executes `npm install --prefix .smithers` without `npm ci`, lock enforcement, or lifecycle-script suppression. When the runner path exists, lines 510-512 and 531-540 accept it solely via `existsSync`, before any regular-file, ownership, symlink, or provenance check. Lines 552-561 also prepend the project-local bin directory to `PATH`. The generated workflow at lines 768-786 imports the project-owned `.smithers/agents` module. Initialization preserves existing files unless forced (`packages/runtime/src/init.ts:161-179`), while `publicInitPaths` at lines 218-220 removes Smithers paths from the returned initialization inventory. Tests at `packages/runtime/test/runtime.test.ts:822-890` explicitly exercise local-binary selection and automatic installation. `.smithers/` is ignored by default, and the documented execution model trusts agents, but that does not make a floating first install reproducible or establish the provenance of hidden runtime plumbing.
issues.mitigation: Ship the workflow runner as an integrity-checked application dependency, or generate an exact lockfile with registry integrity hashes and install with a frozen mechanism such as `npm ci`. Disable dependency lifecycle scripts where compatible and verify the installed package provenance. Before execution, require the runner to be a regular file inside the expected installation, reject symlinks and unexpected ownership/permissions, and validate it against the locked package contents. Deterministically regenerate runtime plumbing or require explicit review of preserved files. Include all generated and preserved Smithers paths in initialization and validation output.

issues.title: M-01
issues.summary: Raw workflow inputs, process arguments, runner output, and agent errors cross persistence and external-telemetry boundaries without comprehensive redaction. Secrets embedded in otherwise legitimate operator input or error text can remain in run evidence, process listings, or provider telemetry.
issues.evidence: `packages/runtime/src/smithers.ts:228-237` writes `operator_prompt` and `operator_input` directly to `smithers/input.json`. Lines 243-260 embed the entire serialized input in the workflow runner's `--input` process argument. `smithersDisplayCommand` at lines 426-428 retains every argument, and lines 272-278 persist that command plus raw stdout and stderr in `submission.json`. The expected raw persistence is asserted by `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts:264-269` and `packages/runtime/test/runtime.test.ts:740-748`. Workflow failures are copied from event payloads at `packages/runtime/src/workflow-sync.ts:893-946` and stored as `state.json` `last_error` at lines 671-692 without redaction. `packages/evals/src/node-telemetry.ts:242-254` reconstructs an external node event using that unredacted state error; `packages/evals/src/reporters/langsmith.ts:113-123` and `braintrust.ts:140-163` transmit it. In contrast, event creation explicitly redacts payloads in `packages/artifacts/src/events.ts:78-106`, showing an inconsistent boundary. The text redactor in `packages/security/src/sensitive-redaction.ts:38-80` recognizes Bearer credentials, URI credentials, exact no-whitespace `key=value` assignments, and a limited set of token formats, but misses common colon-separated, whitespace-separated, and Basic-authorization forms. A read-only synthetic probe corroborated that four such representative forms remained unchanged while the Bearer form was redacted. This conflicts with `docs/security.md:7-14`, which states that run artifacts redact secret-looking values before persistence.
issues.mitigation: Do not place workflow input JSON on the command line; pass it through a protected file descriptor, stdin, or a short-lived mode-0600 file and remove it as soon as submission completes. Persist only a recursively redacted evidence copy unless raw retention is explicitly enabled and encrypted. Redact command arrays, stdout, stderr, state errors, submission evidence, and telemetry immediately before their respective boundaries. Expand structured detection to cover colon syntax, whitespace around separators, authorization header schemes, multiline values, and relevant provider token formats. Prefer provenance-aware sensitive-value tracking over pattern matching alone, and add end-to-end tests proving that input and agent-error secrets cannot reach state files, diagnostics, process arguments, or reporters.

issues.title: M-02
issues.summary: The local dashboard and artifact utilities perform unbounded buffering, recursive enumeration, parsing, and hashing of agent-controlled artifacts. Oversized logs, reports, event journals, request bodies, or deep artifact trees can exhaust memory or monopolize the Node.js event loop.
issues.evidence: `packages/dashboard/src/index.ts:653-687` recursively enumerates every artifact for an attempt, loads every file fully with `readFileSync`, and hashes it synchronously. The same response also loads complete stdout, stderr, rendered prompts, and transcript JSON. The report endpoint at lines 719-745 loads complete Markdown and JSON reports. `packages/artifacts/src/safe-paths.ts:209-245` implements recursive `listSafeFiles` without depth, file-count, or cumulative-size limits. `packages/artifacts/src/events.ts:109-132` reads and splits the complete event journal before applying its record-count limit. `packages/dashboard/src/index.ts:1595-1612` buffers an entire HTTP request body before parsing it, and `sendJson` at lines 1615-1622 creates another complete serialized response. The dashboard is loopback-only and mutations require a session token, which limits remote exposure, but agent artifacts are a normal untrusted/variable-size input to this local operator process. A single large artifact or sufficiently deep/wide output tree can therefore cause local availability loss.
issues.mitigation: Define and enforce per-file, per-request, per-attempt, and per-run byte limits, along with artifact count and directory-depth limits. Hash files with streaming APIs and expose metadata-only records for oversized files. Tail or page logs, cap Markdown/JSON previews, and parse event journals incrementally from bounded ranges rather than loading the complete file. Reject oversized request bodies with HTTP 413 while streaming, add request timeouts and cancellation, and avoid constructing full response copies when streaming or pagination is possible. Test behavior with sparse huge files, deeply nested trees, oversized JSON, and very large event journals.

reports.reportMarkdown:
# Anti-patterns breadth security review

## Snapshot and outcome

This review is anchored to the full target commit `c727b264eb50ebc2422f26d8f6afe8e962155680` of `monad-developers/ultrafuzz`, reviewed on 2026-07-13. The checkout contained 298 tracked files and ten TypeScript workspace packages covering artifacts, CLI, configuration, dashboard, evals, prompts, references, runtime, security, and topology.

The review identified two high-severity and two medium-severity issues. No critical issue was confirmed. The dominant risks are trust-boundary errors: project-controlled configuration can select both a secret source and network destination; generated runtime plumbing installs and executes code without deterministic provenance; several secret-bearing values bypass the repository's redaction boundary; and local artifact processing lacks resource limits.

## Methodology

The anti-patterns-breadth methodology was applied across secrets, command/process injection, browser output and XSS, authentication/session handling, cryptography, validation and resource limits, configuration, dependency and supply-chain behavior, API exposure, and file/path handling. Review included entry-point and data-flow tracing through the CLI, runtime, dashboard, eval reporter, reference synchronization, materialization, and artifact persistence paths.

Read-only verification performed against the snapshot included:

- `pnpm lint`, which completed successfully.
- `pnpm audit --prod --json`, which reported zero known vulnerabilities across 45 production dependencies.
- Targeted searches for credential patterns, dangerous process execution, dynamic code execution, unsafe HTML rendering, network destinations, path traversal, symlink handling, and unbounded file/body processing. No probable live credential was identified; a fixture-only key-shaped test value was reviewed and excluded without reproducing it.
- A synthetic redaction probe using non-secret illustrative inputs, which corroborated the source-level parsing gaps described in M-01.
- Verification that the tracked worktree remained clean after all checks.

The documented trusted-agent model was treated as an explicit design constraint, not as a blanket dismissal of configuration, persistence, external-reporting, or dependency-provenance boundaries.

## H-01

**Severity:** High  
**Relevant weaknesses:** CWE-15, CWE-200, CWE-918

The same tracked project configuration controls which environment variable is read and where its value is sent. This composes two individually flexible settings into a credential-exfiltration primitive.

The root `ultrafuzz.toml` is tracked in this snapshot and is loaded for eval commands by `packages/cli/src/command-shared.ts:53-79`. `packages/config/src/loader.ts:381-422` accepts arbitrary strings for `api_key_env`, `workspace_id_env`, and `endpoint`. The resolved configuration schema in `packages/config/src/resolve.ts:49-79` does not describe eval profiles at all, and `validateResolvedConfig` at lines 107-114 performs no URL, hostname, scheme, private-network, redirect, or environment-name policy check.

At publish time, `packages/evals/src/reporters/index.ts:97-122` indexes the process environment with the configured names and passes the resulting values to the reporter alongside the configured endpoint. `packages/evals/src/reporters/langsmith.ts:351-359` sends them as API and tenant headers to the concatenated endpoint. `packages/evals/src/reporters/braintrust.ts:359-367` sends the selected value in an authorization header. Reporter constructors only require a nonempty credential and do not validate the endpoint.

A malicious or compromised repository can therefore change the profile to name any sensitive variable present in the CLI process and point the endpoint to an attacker-controlled server. When an operator invokes live eval reporting or post-hoc publish, the selected value is sent as a credential header. The same primitive allows authenticated requests to internal HTTP services. The explicit publish step lowers likelihood but does not provide meaningful destination or secret-source confirmation.

Recommended remediation:

1. Use fixed provider-specific environment-variable names, or move secret-source selection into trusted user/CLI configuration that is not repository controlled.
2. Allowlist official HTTPS provider hosts by default. Treat a custom endpoint as a separately enabled advanced feature.
3. Reject URL credentials, insecure schemes, malformed/deceptive hosts, loopback, link-local, and private-network destinations unless the operator explicitly authorizes a trusted self-hosted deployment.
4. Validate every redirect destination or disable redirects for credential-bearing calls.
5. Display the final destination hostname before publishing and add regression tests for malicious profiles.

## H-02

**Severity:** High  
**Relevant weaknesses:** CWE-494, CWE-829

Workflow startup crosses a code-provenance boundary without a deterministic lock or executable verification.

`packages/runtime/src/init.ts:187-203` generates `.smithers/package.json` with caret ranges for the workflow runner and supporting packages. It generates no package lock or integrity manifest, and the repository's root `pnpm-lock.yaml` does not cover `smithers-orchestrator`. On a clean initialized target, `packages/runtime/src/smithers.ts:503-525` automatically runs `npm install --prefix .smithers` without frozen resolution, integrity enforcement, or lifecycle-script suppression. A newly published compatible version can therefore be selected and executed on a user's first installation.

There is also a direct local-executable path. Lines 510-512 and 531-540 trust the expected runner path whenever `existsSync` succeeds. The early return occurs before the package path's symlink checks, and no regular-file, ownership, permission, package-integrity, or provenance test is performed. Lines 552-561 prepend the same project-controlled bin directory to `PATH`. The generated workflow at lines 768-786 also imports the project-owned `.smithers/agents` module.

Initialization preserves pre-existing files unless forced (`packages/runtime/src/init.ts:161-179`), while `publicInitPaths` at lines 218-220 filters Smithers paths from the returned created/preserved/overwritten inventory. Tests at `packages/runtime/test/runtime.test.ts:822-890` confirm both project-local binary selection and automatic dependency bootstrap.

The repository documents agents as trusted and ignores `.smithers/` by default. Those facts reduce accidental exposure but do not make the floating dependency install reproducible, prevent a force-tracked or pre-positioned local runner, or make hidden generated plumbing auditable.

Recommended remediation:

1. Ship the runner in the application's locked dependency graph, or generate an exact lockfile with registry integrity hashes and use a frozen install such as `npm ci`.
2. Disable dependency lifecycle scripts where feasible and verify package provenance after installation.
3. Require the executable to be a non-symlink regular file inside a verified package installation, and validate it against locked contents before execution.
4. Do not prepend an unverified project directory to `PATH` while invoking the installer.
5. Deterministically regenerate runtime plumbing or require explicit review of preserved files, and report all generated/preserved Smithers paths to the operator.

## M-01

**Severity:** Medium  
**Relevant weaknesses:** CWE-214, CWE-312, CWE-532

Secret handling is inconsistent across run persistence, process invocation, diagnostics, and eval telemetry.

`packages/runtime/src/smithers.ts:228-237` writes the operator prompt and arbitrary operator input directly to `smithers/input.json`. Lines 243-260 then put the entire serialized input in the child process's `--input` argument. This can expose it through process inspection. `smithersDisplayCommand` at lines 426-428 retains every argument, and lines 272-278 persist that command along with raw runner stdout and stderr in `submission.json`. Tests at `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts:264-269` and `packages/runtime/test/runtime.test.ts:740-748` explicitly assert raw input persistence.

Workflow errors follow another bypass. `packages/runtime/src/workflow-sync.ts:893-946` accepts error/message content from runner events, and lines 671-692 store it as `state.json` `last_error` without redaction. `packages/evals/src/node-telemetry.ts:242-254` reconstructs a provider event using that state value. Both reporters transmit the error (`packages/evals/src/reporters/langsmith.ts:113-123` and `braintrust.ts:140-163`). This bypasses the event-journal redaction performed in `packages/artifacts/src/events.ts:78-106`.

The pattern redactor also has coverage gaps. `packages/security/src/sensitive-redaction.ts:38-80` recognizes several provider formats, Bearer credentials, credential-bearing URLs, and assignment strings with an exact no-whitespace equals sign. Common colon-separated fields, whitespace around equals signs, and other authorization schemes do not match. A read-only probe with synthetic inputs confirmed these forms remained unchanged. Structured objects receive better protection because sensitive key names are replaced at lines 83-96, but free-form prompts, command output, and error text do not have that structure.

This is especially important because `docs/security.md:7-14` states that run artifacts redact secret-looking values before persistence. Run files use restrictive creation modes, and external publishing is explicit, so the issue is medium rather than high; nevertheless, the stated persistence boundary is not consistently enforced.

Recommended remediation:

1. Pass workflow input through stdin, a protected descriptor, or a short-lived mode-0600 file instead of a process argument.
2. Persist only a recursively redacted evidence representation unless encrypted raw retention is deliberately enabled.
3. Apply redaction independently at every sink: commands, stdout/stderr, state errors, diagnostics, submission evidence, and reporter payloads.
4. Extend free-text parsing for colon syntax, whitespace around separators, multiline values, authorization schemes, and relevant token formats.
5. Track known sensitive values by provenance and redact exact occurrences, rather than relying only on token-shape heuristics.
6. Add end-to-end tests showing that synthetic secrets cannot reach process arguments, run state, diagnostics, or remote reporters.

## M-02

**Severity:** Medium  
**Relevant weakness:** CWE-400

Agent-controlled artifacts can cause unbounded synchronous work and memory allocation in the dashboard process.

`packages/dashboard/src/index.ts:653-687` calls `listSafeFiles` for every attempt, reads every artifact completely to calculate its hash, and then reads complete stdout, stderr, rendered prompt, and transcript files. The report endpoint at lines 719-745 reads complete Markdown and JSON reports. `packages/artifacts/src/safe-paths.ts:209-245` recursively walks without depth, file-count, or cumulative-byte limits.

The event path has the same pattern. `packages/artifacts/src/events.ts:109-132` calls `readFileSync`, splits the complete event journal, and only then applies its record-count limit. The request path at `packages/dashboard/src/index.ts:1595-1612` buffers all body chunks before parsing JSON. Response serialization at lines 1615-1622 creates another complete in-memory representation.

The dashboard's loopback binding, origin/host checks, and mutation token are useful controls and reduce remote exploitability. The relevant attacker-controlled input is instead the normal output of an agentic workflow: a failed or adversarial agent can produce large logs, reports, journals, or a deep artifact tree. Loading the affected view can then exhaust memory or block the single Node.js event loop.

Recommended remediation:

1. Enforce request, file, artifact-count, directory-depth, per-attempt, and cumulative run limits.
2. Compute hashes with streams and return metadata-only records for oversized files.
3. Tail and paginate logs and event journals; seek from known offsets instead of reading the complete file.
4. Cap report and JSON previews and avoid parsing oversized content in the dashboard process.
5. Return HTTP 413 as soon as a streamed body exceeds the configured limit, with request timeouts and cancellation.
6. Exercise the limits with sparse huge files, deep trees, large JSON objects, and high-volume journals.

## Existing controls and negative findings

The snapshot contains several effective defenses that materially constrained the findings:

- File materialization is explicit, copy-only, path constrained, and protected against traversal and symlink escapes.
- Reference catalogs restrict repositories to GitHub owner/repository identifiers, require full commit SHAs, validate reference paths, and record digests.
- Event creation recursively redacts payloads, and durable artifact writers generally use restrictive file modes.
- The dashboard binds to loopback, validates local host/origin values, uses a random mutation token, and compares it in constant time.
- Eval artifact uploads have allowlist, sensitivity, and size-policy controls.
- No dynamic `eval`/`Function` execution or unsafe React HTML insertion was identified in reviewed production sources.
- The production dependency audit reported no known advisories at review time.

## Limitations

The repository's normal build, typecheck, and test scripts build dependencies and remove or create `dist`/`dist-test` trees. They were not invoked because the assignment required the target checkout to remain read-only. Linting, dependency audit, source-level tracing, and narrowly scoped read-only probes were used instead. No live external-provider request, registry installation, destructive materialization, or network exposure test was performed. Dependency-audit results reflect registry advisory data available at review time and do not prove the absence of unpublished or application-specific vulnerabilities.

issues.title: L-01
issues.summary: Node error/diagnostic text (state.json `last_error`) is persisted and forwarded to optional third-party eval telemetry without passing through the secret-redaction that the project applies to its event journal, so a secret embedded in an agent/workflow error message can be written at rest and egressed unredacted.
issues.evidence: The redaction choke point is the event journal only: packages/artifacts/src/events.ts applies redactValue()/redactSecretsInValue() to event payload and provenance (lines 91, 100, 106, 176). State is written raw: packages/artifacts/src/state.ts writeRunState()->writeJsonDurable() (lines 148-149) performs no redaction, and last_error (field at line 54) is set directly from unredacted sources in packages/runtime/src/workflow-sync.ts (evidence.error at 658 and 756; diagnostics.map(d=>d.message) at 821; propagated at 677). packages/runtime/src/smithers.ts routes only captured stdout/stderr through sanitizedDiagnosticText()->redactSecretsInText() (lines 484-491) — not evidence.error. That same last_error is then transmitted to external providers: packages/evals/src/node-telemetry.ts emits node-finished with error: nodeState.last_error (line 250), consumed by packages/evals/src/reporters/braintrust.ts onNodeEvent (error at ~155, sent via Bearer request at 359-367) and packages/evals/src/reporters/langsmith.ts (error at ~122, sent via x-api-key at 351-360). Redaction unit tests exist for the event path (packages/artifacts/test/artifacts.test.ts:106-141) but none assert last_error redaction. docs/security.md states 'Run artifacts redact secret-looking values before persistence', which state.json's last_error does not honor.
issues.mitigation: Route error/diagnostic strings through the shared redactSecretsInText()/redactSecretsInValue() helper before they are stored in state.json and before they leave via reporter.onNodeEvent (or redact centrally when serializing RunState). Add a regression test asserting a secret-bearing last_error is redacted at rest and in telemetry, matching the existing event-journal redaction tests.

issues.title: L-02
issues.summary: When eval artifact reporting is switched to `upload` mode, raw artifact file bytes (e.g. rendered prompts, transcripts, stdout logs, reports) are streamed inline to a configured external observability provider without applying the secret-redaction used elsewhere. This is opt-in and off by default, but is a defense-in-depth inconsistency.
issues.evidence: packages/evals/src/node-telemetry.ts uploadsForManifest() attaches read: () => fs.promises.readFile(absolutePath) returning unredacted file bytes (lines 303-330); the payload gate is policy.mode === 'upload' && (sensitivity !== 'private' || mode_explicit) (lines 308-309). The reporters inline that content: packages/evals/src/reporters/braintrust.ts onArtifact sends content: inlinePayload for textual files <=262144 bytes (lines 202-224); packages/evals/src/reporters/langsmith.ts onArtifact does the same (lines 162-182). No redaction pass is applied to the read() bytes. Exposure is bounded by opt-in defaults: default eval provider is 'none' (packages/config/src/defaults.ts:29), artifact mode defaults to manifest-only and private targets are forced to manifest-only unless explicitly overridden (packages/evals/src/suite.ts:147,152-153; packages/evals/src/types.ts:64-77), and the shipped suite marks targets sensitivity: private (.ultrafuzz/evals/bug-finding.yml).
issues.mitigation: Apply redactSecretsInText() to textual artifact payloads before inline upload (or gate uploads through the same sanitizer used for the event journal), and document that upload mode may transmit unredacted target-derived content to the configured provider so operators can make an informed opt-in.

issues.title: I-01
issues.summary: Scope/applicability note: the repository is a CLI/orchestration tool with no traditional authentication or authorization implementation (no user login, JWT issuance/verification, OAuth2/OIDC, password storage, server-side user sessions, RBAC, or rate-limited auth endpoints), so most of method-02's AuthN/AuthZ pattern checklist is not applicable and could not be exercised.
issues.evidence: A repository-wide search for auth primitives (jsonwebtoken/jwt.sign/verify, passport, express-session, bcrypt/argon2, OAuth strategies, login/refresh/logout endpoints, RBAC middleware) returned no product implementations; matches are limited to the method document itself and to unrelated identifiers. The product's own model is documented as a 'trusted local execution model' (docs/security.md; README.md 'Trust model' section) rather than an authenticated multi-user service. Method-02's supplementary resources referenced in SKILL.md (references/jwt-best-practices.md, references/oauth2-flows.md, references/session-security.md, assets/auth-security-checklist.md, assets/password-policy-template.md, scripts/token-validator.ts) are not present in the method directory (only /tmp/ultrafuzz-fable-executor/methods/method-02/SKILL.md exists), so the checklist was applied from the SKILL.md body alone.
issues.mitigation: No action required for the current architecture. If a hosted/multi-user dashboard or remote API is ever introduced, adopt the SKILL's patterns then (short-lived tokens, httpOnly/secure/sameSite cookies, server-side authorization, auth-endpoint rate limiting, MFA).

issues.title: I-02
issues.summary: The localhost dashboard's read-only GET endpoints require only a loopback check (Host/Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site), not the session token, so any local process or an allowed-origin page can read run data, findings, prompts, and the project's ultrafuzz.toml content. This is acceptable under the documented single-user trusted-local model; the config exposure is limited to environment-variable names (not secret values).
issues.evidence: packages/dashboard/src/index.ts handle() applies requireLocalRequest() to all /api routes (lines 187-195) but only mutation routes additionally call requireMutation()/constant-time session-token check (requireMutation 1568-1574; constantTimeEqual 1589-1593; token = crypto.randomBytes(32) at line 151; validateLoopbackHost 1546-1551; loopback/Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site enforcement 1553-1566). session() returns the sessionToken over a loopback-only GET (374-381). configDetail() serves the raw ultrafuzz.toml (783-796); because credentials are stored only as env-var names (see I-04 context: agents.ts apiKeyEnv, resolve.ts serializes api_key_env not values), no secret value is exposed. Tests confirm the model: mutations return 401 without the token and non-loopback Host is 403 (packages/dashboard/test/dashboard.test.ts:92-125). The token is never rotated for the server lifetime.
issues.mitigation: Document that read endpoints are authorized by loopback only and that the dashboard assumes a single-user trusted local host. If stronger isolation is ever needed, require the session token on read endpoints too and/or bind to a per-run unguessable path prefix.

issues.title: I-03
issues.summary: The target-repository E2E GitHub Actions workflow triggers on an unqualified `pull_request` event and references a repository secret to run long agent jobs. GitHub's default fork-secret withholding plus explicit masking and stdin-based login prevent direct credential leakage, but the trigger causes agent jobs to be attempted on every PR.
issues.evidence: .github/workflows/target-e2e.yml triggers on pull_request, push (main), and workflow_dispatch (lines 1-6) with permissions: contents: read. Steps reference secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY (lines 67, 105, 110, 153), mask it with '::add-mask::' (line 73), pipe it via stdin to codex login --with-api-key rather than as an argument (line 106), and guard on an empty value (lines 69-70) — so fork PRs (which receive no secrets) fail fast instead of leaking. The job has a 120-minute timeout and runs agents against external target repos.
issues.mitigation: Scope credential-bearing E2E runs to non-fork/trusted contexts — e.g. gate on github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork == false, move to a protected Actions Environment with required reviewers, or restrict to workflow_dispatch/push — to avoid attempting privileged agent jobs on arbitrary PRs while keeping the current masking/stdin practices.

reports.reportMarkdown:
# Defensive Review — method-02: Authentication & Authorization Implementation Patterns

- **Target checkout:** /tmp/ultrafuzz-fable-executor/repository (Ultrafuzz — agentic orchestrator for smart-contract fuzzing)
- **Snapshot commit:** `c727b264eb50ebc2422f26d8f6afe8e962155680` — "Upgrade Smithers and require task summaries (#32)", 2026-07-13, branch `main`, working tree clean, 298 tracked files.
- **Method:** method-02 (`auth-implementation-patterns-review`), entry point `methods/method-02/SKILL.md`, read in full.
- **Intended model:** claude-fable-5 (effort max). No provider refusal/degradation occurred; the intended primary produced this report.
- **Handling:** Review-only. No files edited, no artifacts written into the checkout, no git/remote writes. Repository content treated as untrusted data. No credential values reproduced.

---

## 1. Method application and scope

SKILL.md prescribes reviewing authentication/authorization code against industry patterns: JWT issuance/verification and refresh-token flows, session-based auth, OAuth2/OIDC social login, RBAC/permission/ownership authorization, password security (bcrypt/argon2 + strength policy), rate limiting, secure cookies, CSRF protection, secret rotation, security-event logging, and MFA.

**Applicability finding (I-01):** Ultrafuzz is a local CLI/orchestration monorepo, not an authenticated multi-user service. It contains **no** user login, JWT issuance/verification, OAuth2/OIDC, password hashing, server-side user sessions, RBAC middleware, or rate-limited auth endpoints. The product explicitly documents a *trusted local execution model* (docs/security.md; README.md "Trust model"). Therefore most of the SKILL's AuthN/AuthZ checklist is **not applicable** and could not be exercised against product code.

I narrowed the review to the auth/authz-relevant surfaces that genuinely exist:
1. **Control-plane authentication/authorization** — the local dashboard HTTP server (a session-token + CSRF/DNS-rebind model).
2. **Credential handling** — how LLM-provider and eval-provider secrets are referenced, resolved, passed to subprocesses, and (not) persisted.
3. **Secret hygiene / redaction** — the pipeline that scrubs secret-looking values before persistence and egress.
4. **Authorization for side effects** — filesystem write authorization (path policy, materialize/clean policy) and the dashboard command allowlist.

**Resource limitation:** SKILL.md references supplementary files (`references/jwt-best-practices.md`, `references/oauth2-flows.md`, `references/session-security.md`, `assets/auth-security-checklist.md`, `assets/password-policy-template.md`, `scripts/token-validator.ts`). None are present in the method directory (only `SKILL.md` exists), so the methodology was applied from the SKILL.md body, which contains the full inline pattern catalog and best-practice/pitfall lists.

---

## 2. Repository overview

pnpm/TypeScript workspace with packages: `artifacts`, `cli`, `config`, `dashboard`, `evals`, `prompts`, `references`, `runtime`, `security`, `topology`. Relevant to this method:
- `packages/security` — path policy, materialize policy, secret-redaction primitives.
- `packages/config` — config loading/resolution, config redaction, agent credential schema.
- `packages/artifacts` — event journal + run-state persistence (redaction choke point for events).
- `packages/dashboard` — loopback HTTP control plane.
- `packages/evals` — optional third-party telemetry reporters (Braintrust, LangSmith).

---

## 3. Positive controls observed (mapped to SKILL best practices)

These are working, test-backed controls; they are reported for completeness and are not defects.

- **Credentials referenced by name, never stored (SKILL: "Never store plain secrets", "Rotate secrets").** Agent/eval-provider config stores only the *environment-variable name* (`api_key_env`, `workspace_id_env`), validated as an env identifier; the secret value is resolved from the environment at runtime. Evidence: `packages/config/src/agents.ts` (discriminated union on `auth: 'api-key' | 'subscription'`, `apiKeyEnv` = env name, lines 12,15-26), `packages/config/src/resolve.ts` serializes `api_key_env`/`workspace_id_env` names only (149-181), `packages/runtime/src/templates/smithers/agents/codex.tsx` reads the env value at runtime and blanks `OPENAI_API_KEY` for subscription auth to avoid stray-key leakage (lines 15-28). A defensive `redactResolvedConfig` also redacts any secret-looking scalar before config snapshots are written (`packages/config/src/redaction.ts`; used in `runtime/src/init.ts`, `runtime/src/plan-run.ts`).
- **Secret redaction pipeline with tests.** `packages/security/src/sensitive-redaction.ts` covers token families (OpenAI `sk-`/`sk-ant-`, GitHub `ghp_`/`github_pat_`, GitLab, HuggingFace, Slack), AWS access keys, JWT-shaped triples, `Bearer` headers, URL basic-auth credentials, `key=value` secrets, and PEM private keys; applied to the event journal (`packages/artifacts/src/events.ts:176`) and diagnostics (`packages/runtime/src/validate.ts`). Tests assert redaction of these families (`packages/artifacts/test/artifacts.test.ts:106-141`). No real secrets are committed (the only secret-shaped string in tracked files is a canonical *example* AWS key inside a redaction unit test).
- **Dashboard control-plane authZ (SKILL: secure cookies/CSRF, server-side checks).** `packages/dashboard/src/index.ts` binds to loopback only (`validateLoopbackHost`, 1546-1551), rejects non-loopback `Host`/`Origin` and cross-site `Sec-Fetch-Site` on every `/api` route (`requireLocalRequest`, 1553-1566) — a DNS-rebinding/CSRF defense — and gates all state-changing routes behind a 256-bit random session token compared in constant time (`requireMutation`/`constantTimeEqual`, 1568-1593; token from `crypto.randomBytes(32)`, line 151). Mutations require explicit confirmation for destructive commands (materialize/clean). Tests confirm 401 without token and 403 for non-loopback host (`packages/dashboard/test/dashboard.test.ts:92-125`).
- **No shell/command injection in the dashboard.** Dashboard commands are a fixed allowlist (`SUPPORTED_COMMANDS`) dispatched to typed runtime functions; the assembled `argv` is display-only and no shell is invoked (`executeCommand`, 1211-1303). Run IDs and node IDs are validated via `validateSafeId`.
- **Robust filesystem authorization (SKILL: server-side authorization / resource-scope enforcement analog).** `packages/security/src/path-policy.ts` blocks traversal, absolute/UNC/`file:` paths, backslashes, control chars, reserved Windows names, and (via `resolvePathInside`/realpath) symlink escapes. `packages/security/src/materialize-policy.ts` rejects glob/implicit selections, git metadata, the `.ultrafuzz` product surface, and sensitive destinations (`.env*`, `secrets.*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `secrets/`, `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.gcloud`, `.azure`), and constrains materialization to `dry-run`/`unstaged-working-tree` (never stage/commit/push). Dashboard file reads use `assertPathInside`/`assertRegularFileInside`/`assertNoSymlinkComponents`; static assets are confined to the `public/` dir. Backed by `packages/security/test/path-policy.test.ts` and `materialize-policy.test.ts`.
- **CI secret hygiene.** `.github/workflows/target-e2e.yml` masks the API key (`::add-mask::`, line 73) and logs in via stdin (`printenv ... | codex login --with-api-key`, line 106) rather than passing it as an argument.

---

## 4. Findings

Severity uses the standard scale. No critical/high issues were identified; inventing auth vulnerabilities absent an auth surface would be inaccurate. The substantive gaps are two low-severity secret-redaction inconsistencies; the remainder are informational scoping/hardening notes.

### L-01 — Error/diagnostic text bypasses the redaction applied to the event journal (persisted at rest and forwarded to optional telemetry)
- **Severity:** low
- **Where:** `packages/artifacts/src/state.ts` (148-149, field `last_error` at 54), `packages/runtime/src/workflow-sync.ts` (658, 677, 756, 821), `packages/runtime/src/smithers.ts` (484-491), `packages/evals/src/node-telemetry.ts` (250), `packages/evals/src/reporters/braintrust.ts` (~155, 359-367), `packages/evals/src/reporters/langsmith.ts` (~122, 351-360).
- **Detail:** The project's single redaction choke point is the event journal (`events.ts` redacts payload/provenance). `writeRunState()` writes `state.json` verbatim, and `last_error` is populated directly from `evidence.error` and joined diagnostic messages, none of which are passed through `redactSecretsInText()`. Only captured workflow stdout/stderr in diagnostic `details` are sanitized (`sanitizedDiagnosticText`). That unredacted `last_error` is then transmitted to any configured eval provider as the node `error` field. If a secret surfaces in an agent/workflow error line (e.g. an upstream 401 echoing an `Authorization: Bearer ...` header), it is stored unredacted and can egress. This contradicts docs/security.md ("Run artifacts redact secret-looking values before persistence"). No test asserts `last_error` redaction, unlike the event path.
- **Exploitability:** low — requires a secret to appear in error/diagnostic text; egress additionally requires the opt-in telemetry provider (see L-02 gating). Local `state.json` lives under gitignored `.ultrafuzz/**`.
- **Mitigation:** Redact error/diagnostic strings through the shared helper before writing `state.json` and before `reporter.onNodeEvent`; add a regression test mirroring the event-journal redaction tests.

### L-02 — Eval artifact payloads uploaded to third-party providers are not redacted (opt-in)
- **Severity:** low
- **Where:** `packages/evals/src/node-telemetry.ts` (303-330; gate 308-309), `packages/evals/src/reporters/braintrust.ts` (202-224), `packages/evals/src/reporters/langsmith.ts` (162-182).
- **Detail:** In `upload` mode the uploader hands reporters raw file bytes via `read: () => fs.promises.readFile(absolutePath)`, and reporters inline textual content (<=256 KiB) into provider requests without redaction — even though the event stream is redacted. Artifact files (rendered prompts, transcripts, stdout logs, reports) can contain target-derived or injected secrets.
- **Exploitability:** low — doubly opt-in: default provider is `none` (`config/src/defaults.ts:29`), default artifact mode is `manifest-only`, private targets are forced to manifest-only unless explicitly overridden (`evals/src/suite.ts:147,152-153`; `types.ts:64-77`), and the shipped suite marks targets `sensitivity: private`.
- **Mitigation:** Apply `redactSecretsInText()` to textual payloads before inline upload (or reuse the event-journal sanitizer), and document that `upload` mode may transmit unredacted content to the configured provider.

### I-02 — Dashboard read endpoints authorized by loopback only (no session token); config content served
- **Severity:** informational
- **Where:** `packages/dashboard/src/index.ts` (handle 187-195; session 374-381; configDetail 783-796; token 151).
- **Detail:** GET/read endpoints require only the loopback/Origin/Sec-Fetch checks, not the session token, so any local process or allowed-origin page can read run data, findings, prompts, events, and the raw `ultrafuzz.toml`. Acceptable under the documented single-user trusted-local model; importantly, `ultrafuzz.toml` holds only env-var *names*, so no secret value is exposed. The token is not rotated for the server lifetime.
- **Mitigation:** Document the loopback-only read authorization and single-user assumption; if stronger isolation is later required, require the token on reads and/or bind the dashboard behind a per-run unguessable path prefix.

### I-03 — E2E workflow uses an unqualified `pull_request` trigger with a repository secret
- **Severity:** informational
- **Where:** `.github/workflows/target-e2e.yml` (triggers 1-6; secret refs 67,105,110,153; mask 73; stdin login 106; guard 69-70).
- **Detail:** The credential-bearing, 120-minute agent workflow triggers on every PR. GitHub withholds secrets from fork PRs (the empty-value guard then fails fast) and the key is masked and provided via stdin, so there is no direct credential leak; the residual concern is that privileged agent jobs are *attempted* on arbitrary PRs.
- **Mitigation:** Gate credential-bearing runs to non-fork/trusted contexts (e.g. `head.repo.fork == false`, a protected Actions Environment with required reviewers, or `push`/`workflow_dispatch` only) while retaining the current masking/stdin practices.

### I-01 — No traditional auth surface (scope narrowing)
- **Severity:** informational — see Section 1. The method's AuthN/AuthZ pattern checklist (JWT, OAuth2, sessions, RBAC, password policy, auth rate limiting, MFA) is not applicable to the current architecture. Recorded so the near-empty AuthN result is not mistaken for missing coverage.

---

## 5. SKILL best-practice/pitfall checklist mapping

| SKILL item | Status in Ultrafuzz |
|---|---|
| Never store plain secrets; hash passwords | N/A (no passwords). Secrets referenced by env-var name, never stored — good. |
| Use HTTPS in transit | Local loopback dashboard (plaintext acceptable on 127.0.0.1); provider egress uses HTTPS endpoints (braintrust.dev / smith.langchain.com). |
| Short-lived access tokens / expiration | N/A (no issued user tokens). Dashboard session token is per-process, loopback-scoped. |
| Secure cookies (httpOnly/secure/sameSite) | N/A — dashboard uses a header token (`x-ultrafuzz-session`), not cookies; CSRF handled via Origin/Sec-Fetch + token. |
| Validate all input server-side | Strong — zod schemas, `validateSafeId`, path/materialize policies. |
| Rate limit auth endpoints | N/A (no auth endpoints); dashboard caps command jobs/output. |
| CSRF protection | Present for mutations (loopback + Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site + constant-time token). |
| Rotate secrets | Supported operationally (env-var indirection; config redaction on snapshot); dashboard token not rotated within a process (informational). |
| Log security events | Dashboard writes an append-only audit log (`dashboard-audit.jsonl`, mode 0o600) for config/topology/prompt edits. |
| MFA | N/A. |
| Pitfall: secrets in logs / client storage | Mostly mitigated by the redaction pipeline; residual gaps are L-01 (error text) and L-02 (artifact upload payloads). |
| Server-side authorization / ownership | Realized as filesystem write authorization (path/materialize policy) and a dashboard command allowlist — strong. |

---

## 6. Methods, coverage, and limitations

- **Coverage:** Read SKILL.md in full; inspected all security/credential/redaction/dashboard/eval-reporter source under `packages/*/src`, config resolution/defaults, event/state persistence, agent credential template, CI workflows, `.gitignore`, and docs/security.md. Ran non-destructive `git` and `grep` checks (secret-pattern scan across tracked files, redaction usage tracing, auth-primitive search) and reviewed the dashboard/redaction/path-policy tests.
- **Not exhaustively analyzed:** the compiled `dist/` outputs (build artifacts, excluded), the large local `smithers.db` runtime database (gitignored, not code), the `smithers-orchestrator` third-party dependency internals, and full runtime behavior of every CLI command (static review only; no campaign executed).
- **Confidence:** L-01/L-02 are code-substantiated with exact call paths; both are bounded by opt-in defaults and the requirement that a secret first appear in the relevant text/file, hence low severity. Informational items are hardening/scoping notes, not defects.
- **Bottom line:** For its documented trusted-local threat model, Ultrafuzz's auth-relevant controls (credential indirection, redaction with tests, loopback+token control plane, and deterministic filesystem authorization) are sound. The actionable improvements are to extend the existing redaction consistently to error text (L-01) and to uploaded artifact payloads (L-02).

issues.title: H-01
issues.summary: The loopback dashboard returns its sole mutation credential to unauthenticated callers. Any process capable of reaching the local TCP port can obtain the token and invoke protected editing and command APIs as the operator.
issues.evidence: In packages/dashboard/src/index.ts:187-194, API requests receive only Host, Origin, and Sec-Fetch-Site locality checks. GET /api/session is then served without authentication at lines 209-211, and session() returns sessionToken at lines 374-380. The same token is accepted by requireMutation at lines 1568-1573 for config and topology writes, prompt creation and editing, and command execution at lines 249-276 and 282-337. Command APIs can launch campaigns with the dashboard process environment, edit trusted prompts/configuration, synchronize references, materialize output, and clean generated files (lines 1163-1303). A read-only audit reproduction against a temporary project received HTTP 200 from unauthenticated GET /api/session, obtained a 64-character capability, and then received HTTP 202 from POST /api/commands/validate using that disclosed capability. Loopback binding limits network exposure but does not distinguish OS users, local processes, containers sharing the network namespace, or server-side request forgery in another local service.
issues.mitigation: Treat loopback locality as transport scoping, not authentication. Generate an operator bearer credential and deliver it out-of-band through the invoking terminal, a mode-0600 per-user file, or an OS-protected local socket. One practical browser flow is to put a one-time bootstrap value in the CLI-printed URL fragment, exchange it once for an authenticated session, remove it from browser history, and require that session for every API route, including reads and event streams. Do not return a usable mutation credential from an unauthenticated endpoint. Prefer Unix-domain sockets or equivalent peer-credential checks where supported. Add tests proving that an unauthenticated local client cannot retrieve configuration, prompts, run evidence, command jobs, or a mutation capability and cannot invoke any command.

issues.title: M-01
issues.summary: Eval provider API credentials can be transmitted to any endpoint named in project configuration, including an attacker-controlled or plaintext HTTP endpoint.
issues.evidence: packages/config/src/loader.ts:381-422 treats each eval provider endpoint as an unconstrained string; normalization in packages/config/src/defaults.ts:130-146 preserves it without URL, scheme, or origin validation. packages/evals/src/reporters/index.ts:97-123 reads the configured environment-variable credential and combines it with the configured endpoint. BraintrustReporter attaches the credential as a Bearer Authorization header to `${apiUrl}${requestPath}` at packages/evals/src/reporters/braintrust.ts:359-367, while LangSmithReporter attaches it as x-api-key at packages/evals/src/reporters/langsmith.ts:351-360. The endpoint and credential-variable name originate from project-level ultrafuzz.toml loaded by packages/cli/src/command-shared.ts:57-79. A synthetic audit check confirmed that endpoint `http://127.0.0.1:9` passes parsing and resolution and that every generated provider request carries the authentication header. No real credential was used or displayed.
issues.mitigation: Parse endpoints as URLs and require HTTPS. Bind each provider credential to an allowlisted provider origin by default. If self-hosted endpoints are necessary, require an explicit operator-controlled opt-in outside project-owned configuration and a separate credential intended for that origin. Reject URL userinfo, ambiguous concatenation, and plaintext HTTP except narrowly scoped development exceptions that cannot access production credentials. Disable redirects or revalidate every redirect destination before forwarding authentication headers. Add tests covering HTTP endpoints, unexpected hosts, malformed URLs, userinfo, cross-origin redirects, and approved custom HTTPS deployments.

reports.reportMarkdown:
# Authentication and Authorization Security Review

Snapshot: `c727b264eb50ebc2422f26d8f6afe8e962155680`

Skill: `auth-implementation-patterns`

Status: Complete for the checked-out commit.

## Executive summary

The review found one high-severity and one medium-severity authentication-related issue. The local dashboard's random session token is cryptographically strong but is issued to every unauthenticated loopback caller, so it does not authenticate an operator or authorize a local principal. A caller that can connect to the port can retrieve the token and use the dashboard process's filesystem and campaign privileges. Separately, eval provider credentials are attached to requests sent to an arbitrary endpoint supplied by project configuration, including plaintext HTTP.

The repository does not implement user passwords, JWTs, refresh tokens, OAuth/OIDC, MFA, account recovery, multi-tenancy, or RBAC. Those portions of the assigned methodology are therefore not applicable. Relevant authentication surfaces are the dashboard capability token, Codex API-key/subscription selection, eval provider credentials, and credentials inherited by workflow execution.

## Scope and methodology

The audit enumerated the 298 tracked files at the target commit and searched the approximately 56,000 tracked lines for authentication, authorization, token, session, cookie, credential, origin, host, and provider-header behavior. Detailed review covered the dashboard server and frontend, CLI dashboard command, agent authentication configuration and generated Codex adapter, runtime environment propagation, eval configuration loading, provider selection, Braintrust and LangSmith request implementations, tests, security documentation, and GitHub workflow credential use.

Control flow was traced from external input to authorization decisions and privileged sinks:

- Dashboard request → locality checks → session issuance → mutation check → file or command operation.
- `ultrafuzz.toml` → eval provider profile → environment-variable lookup → provider endpoint → authentication header.
- Agent auth mode → generated Codex adapter → workflow runner environment.

Read-only validation performed during the audit included:

- ESLint over the dashboard, auth configuration, eval reporter, Codex adapter, and workflow-runner files; it completed successfully.
- The compiled dashboard test suite; all 4 tests passed.
- Scoped eval reporter tests; all 12 tests passed.
- Scoped eval configuration tests; all 5 tests passed.
- A temporary-project dashboard reproduction confirming unauthenticated token issuance followed by acceptance of a token-protected command.
- A synthetic provider reproduction confirming that a plaintext custom endpoint is accepted and receives an authentication header. It used no real credential or external request.
